content:
Reddit announced two upcoming changes that some long-time users may not be happy about.

The company has already imposed one restriction on old Reddit, and is now announcing a second. Additionally, RSS support will be ending…

Old Reddit

Reddit made major changes to its user interface back in 2018, which drew strong opposition from users who preferred the old version. In response to these voices, the platform promised at the time that it would keep offering what later became known as "Old Reddit" for as long as people still used it.

In August this year, the company first changed this policy, requiring users of Old Reddit to be logged in. Now they are announcing that the old interface will only be available to users who have used it within the past six months, with new users no longer able to access it.

Reddit said both measures are aimed at reducing AI scraping on its platform (though if you're willing to pay for a license, the issue doesn't seem to be one).

RSS Feed Support Ending

The ending of RSS feed support is also based on the same reasoning.

For subreddits relying on RSS to maintain their moderation workflows, this change could have an especially large impact. Reddit says they are aware of this and suggests that moderators use Devvit apps, such as Discord Relay instead.

User Reaction Cool

Reading the comments in the comments section shows that many long-time users are very unhappy with these latest developments.

What are your thoughts on these latest changes? Feel free to share them in the comments.
